_comment: The grammar terms the app names, in one place. On a tag the Arabic term stands alone: مبتدأ, منصوب. Its English is here, in the glossary at the foot of the Nahw page, in the order a nahw book teaches them: kinds of word, endings, sentences, then the roles grouped as the books group them. 'types' and 'cases' are keyed by the string the backend sends and also give the tags their Arabic; 'sections' hold every role and tarkeeb term the page can print, once each (tests/test_rule_engine.py checks it against roles.json and tarkeeb.json). lib/grammarTerms.js is the only reader.

ism.meaning: A noun: a person, thing, place, quality or name. It takes case endings.

fi'l.meaning: A verb: something done, in past, present or command form. The past form never changes its ending; the present one does.

harf.meaning: A particle: a small word with no meaning of its own until joined to others, such as في, و, لم. Its ending never changes.

damir.meaning: A pronoun: هو, أنت, or one attached to a word like the ـه in كتابه.

zarf.meaning: A word for when or where: قبل, عند, فوق.

raf'.meaning: The ending for a subject: a ضمة on one noun, و on a sound masculine plural.

nasb.meaning: The ending for an object and for what comes after إن: a فتحة on one noun.

jarr.meaning: The ending after a preposition or as the second word of a مضاف pair: a كسرة on one noun.

jazm.meaning: The ending of a present verb after لم, the لا that forbids, the لام of command and their like: a سكون, or a dropped final letter.

mabni.meaning: Fixed. The ending never changes whatever the word is doing: past verbs, pronouns, particles.

terms.meaning: A sentence that starts with a verb: كتب الطالب.
A sentence that starts with a noun and has no verb at its head: الطالب مجتهد.
A sentence that asks a question, with هل, أ, متى, أين and their like.
A sentence that calls someone with يا, as in يا محمد.
The one doing the verb: كتب الطالبُ.
The word standing in for the doer when the verb is passive: كُتِبَ الدرسُ.
What a sentence without a verb is about: الطالبُ مجتهد.
What is said about the مبتدأ, as in الطالب مجتهدٌ.
كان or one of its sisters (صار, أصبح, ليس...). It comes before a مبتدأ and خبر and changes the خبر to منصوب.
The مبتدأ after كان. It stays مرفوع.
The خبر after كان. It becomes منصوب.
كاد or one of its sisters (أوشك, عسى...): something nearly or about to happen. Its خبر is a present verb.
The مبتدأ after كاد. It stays مرفوع.
The present verb after كاد saying what nearly happened.
إن or one of its sisters (أن, كأن, لكن, ليت, لعل). It comes before a مبتدأ and خبر and changes the مبتدأ to منصوب.
The مبتدأ after إن. It becomes منصوب.
The خبر after إن. It stays مرفوع.
The لا that denies a whole kind: لا ريبَ فيه. It works like إن.
The ما that denies the way ليس does, as in ما هذا بشرًا. Its خبر is منصوب.
The one the verb is done to: كتب الطالب الدرسَ.
The verb's own noun repeated to stress it or say how: ضربته ضربًا.
When or where the verb happened: سافرت ليلًا.
A مفعول فيه that says when: يومَ, ليلًا, قبلَ.
A مفعول فيه that says where: عندَ, فوقَ, أمامَ.
What the verb happened alongside, after a و meaning 'with': سرت والنيلَ.
The state someone was in while the verb happened: جاء راكبًا. It has no ال.
A word that makes a vague one clear: عشرون كتابًا. It has no ال.
The one called after يا, as in يا محمدُ. It is منصوب when it is the first word of a مضاف pair, otherwise usually مبني on a ضمة.
The one left out after إلا, as in جاء القوم إلا زيدًا.
A preposition: في, على, من, إلى, بـ, لـ. The noun after it is مجرور.
A preposition and the noun after it, read together as one unit: في البيتِ.
The first word of an 'X of Y' pair: كتابُ الطالب. It takes no ال.
The second word of an 'X of Y' pair: كتاب الطالبِ. Always مجرور.
A مضاف and its مضاف إليه read together as one unit.

sections.title: Followers: they copy the word before them

terms.meaning: The noun a صفة describes.
Describes the noun before it and copies its gender, number, ال and ending: الطالبُ المجتهدُ.
A موصوف and its صفة read together as one unit.
A joining word: و, ف, ثم, أو.
The word after a حرف عطف. It copies the ending of the word it is joined to.
A word that stresses the one before it: جاء القوم كلُّهم.
A word that renames the one before it: جاء أخوك زيدٌ.
A word like الذي or التي that a clause after it describes.
The clause after a اسم موصول that completes it: الذي نجحَ.
A اسم موصول and its صلة read together as one unit.
A و or ف that starts a fresh sentence rather than joining a word to the one before.

_corpus_pos_comment: The Quranic corpus files every word as N, V or P. Each names the type above it prints as.
